data_status: STRICT MODE: this dataset contains only values that were compared with, or ingested directly from, retrieved sources: JPL (SSD, SBDB, NHATS), NASA (NSSDC fact sheets and mission catalog, Small Spacecraft SoA report 2026, SLS page, Apollo 11 press kit, NTRS papers, data.nasa.gov), ULA, ESA, NIST, and the Launch Library 2 aggregator. Records carry source_authority/confidence where the source is an aggregator or vendor-reported compilation. Recalled, estimated and fictional values (optimizer catalog, costs, engine/vehicle specs without a retrievable source, the user-supplied SpaceX table) are not included. Derived values are computed only from verified inputs and are labelled derived.

record.name: Lyman-Alpha Mapper (LAMP)
record.description: The Lyman-Alpha Mapper (LAMP) is an imaging ultraviolet (UV) spectrometer designed to use low UV light conditions due to starlight and Lyman sky-glow to image the permanently shadowed regions near the Moon's poles. The instrument objectives are to identify and localize exposed water frost and collect landform-scale mapping in permanently shadowed regions, demonstrate the feasibility of starlight and sky-glow illumination for future missions, and assay the lunar atmosphere and its variability. The LAMP instrument is 46 cm long and consists of a telescope entrance aperture, baffles, mirror, slit, double delay line detector and a grating. Detector and command and data handling electronics and the low voltage power supply are housed together with the instrument.
